reviews.review: TICK NOISES AND NUMBERS GO BRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRR

Very fun and fast-paced roguelite FPS with absolutely amazing level design and graphics style. The gun feel is great and combat is really fun. You can try many different builds with 6 different classes that each have their own unique abilities. The soundtrack is also one of the best I have ever heard and it fits the gameplay perfectly.
You should definitely try it.
Damn, these robots really are on a quest.

A must for any game collection at this price.

This might be my favorite roguelike FPS, and one of my favorite shooters ever made. They NAIL the feeling of constantly finding little ways to enhance and optimize your run - upgrades gained by leveling up over the course of a run feel intuitive and impactful, the flow of currency is steady enough that you usually have some interesting choices to make at the start of each map, and the rolls on the guns feel significant and interesting. 

But what *really* brings it all together is the level of care put into the production - an FPS lives and dies by how its weapons feel, in my opinion, particularly when you're expected to run through similar maps over and over again, and this game just *feels* good to play. These weapons are *fantastic* - almost every one of them feels great to use, and the ones I don't like are a matter of personal preference, not some deficiency on the behalf of the developers. Big explosive weapons have oomph, the shotguns all feel powerful, the machine guns sound and look great; even the class abilities feel great to use, including the melee swings. (DEADLINK, take note.) 

Movement is snappy enough to have a skill ceiling without ever feeling overly chaotic, and your slowly expanding pool of movement options means you're still discovering new things late into the game's progression. Moreover, the bright, vivid, cel-shaded palette crossed with simple and easy to read enemy designs means I don't lose track of anything in the chaos of a hectic fight. The fights feel good, too, because Roboquest (usually) ensures you're equipped no matter what to make the fights feel snappy and dangerous - enemies deal enough damage to be a constant threat without being bullet sponges themselves, even if you're not fully kitted out with an optimal build. 

(I consider this crucial: a roguelike should feel good to play even if you don't get lucky with damage upgrades. Roboquest nails this in a way that a lot of games in this genre do not.) 

If I have one critique it's early runs, sans some of the upgrade options unlocked by the meta progression, can feel really punishing. Once you start having more options for weapons and upgrades, giving you a better chance at picks that synergize, things feel a lot less daunting; I'm a self-admitted garbage FPS player and I still managed to eventually clear the highest difficulty currently available, so I think that's a good indication that the game becomes significantly more do-able after some unlocks. 

I picked this up in early access and on release it shot from an occasional amusement to a spot in my top 10 FPS games ever. It nails the best things about roguelikes in a package that deserves way more acclaim than it has, and it's still getting more updates this year. Easily my most recommended game to people.
